## Finding semantics

`supported` means the stated rule is established by the referenced evidence.
`blocked` means an observed rule failure, supplied return/rejection, or an explicit
hold. `unresolved` means missing, ambiguous or unverifiable evidence/definitions.
Every finding records a rule, reason, owner, source references and required repair.
The source index resolves record IDs to source hashes and PDF pages or workbook
sheet/rows. Rule references resolve to policy lines. The original 18 normalization
diagnostics are preserved globally and attached to their claim revisions.

Gross purchase, base capped amount, explicit replacement allowed amount and
converted cents are separate fields. Unknown paid evidence, category, cap or FX
never becomes zero. Personal purchases have known zero entitlement. Monetary
outputs in EUR are integer cents; original-currency decimals remain strings.
Each converted line is rounded decimal half-up before summing. Calculated totals
are gross policy calculations, **not authorized or incrementally payable amounts**.
Shared costs such as C03/C24 retain both occurrences and an owned unresolved
prior-obligation link; exclusion requires the deferred Finance stage.

`eligibility_status` aggregates expense eligibility and identity/date checks.
`approval_status` covers supplied current role responses and packet limitations.
Overall claim `status` also includes historical arrangement failures and original
request holds. `current_at_batch` distinguishes current from historical revisions.
All revisions are rechecked against the selected batch's visible facts; these are
not execution-time snapshots of earlier batches. Global unresolved findings apply
even where individual eligibility or role checks are supported.

Corrections use a full dependency recheck, allowed by policy line 23 and the
stakeholder interview. No claim review is inherited from another revision, even
when totals match. Exact claim and permit subjects/revisions are independent.
Packets must match employee, trip/permit revisions, expense IDs, policy and business
context. Role authority comes from the employee's directory row. Only the joint
budget-owner/supervisor response may cover two roles. Director thresholds use
strictly more than EUR 1,000: trip estimate for permit, calculated entitlement for
claim. Missing entitlement leaves the director requirement unresolved.

Visible valid replies are ordered by business decision time for each role; an
equal-time ambiguity is held. Returns require a concrete repair request; rejects
retain their reason. Invalid, stale and wrong-role imports remain visible and
satisfy no required role. Rejection here does not close a claim or erase money.

Cancellation deliveries are checked for immutable payload conflicts, unique
initiation/confirmation, exact trip/permit targets, directory employee/supervisor
authority, arrival visibility, strictly later confirmation, and own-time effect.
All four observed processes, including no-claim TC122, remain separate. A permit
cancellation leaves its trip active; an old trip cancellation does not affect a
replacement trip. Timely historical permission is retained after cancellation.
Spent costs need an exact `travel_cancellation` Finance exception plus fresh,
post-confirmation cancellation-aware packets. An amount-only exception does not
cover it. Exceptions never approve arrangements or supply payment evidence.

The supplied Budget ledger context subtracts net settled expenditure and only the
unsettled portion of commitments, avoiding double subtraction. Packets must name
the entire supplied department/project/period ledger. Accepted new Finance
requests remain outside this calculation, so budget completeness is unresolved.
Adequate funds do not substitute for a budget-owner response.

## Admission and replay

All deliveries visible at the selected arrival horizon retain their normalized
values, decoded raw cells and source locators. Finance event IDs form a separate
namespace from business cancellation activity IDs. Immutable Finance payloads
compare all decoded raw fields and normalized values except arrival batch.

An exact redelivery has no additional monetary or commitment effect. A later
conflicting payload cannot replace the earlier admitted event or erase its money;
all affected requests are held and exact net becomes unresolved. Conflicting
payloads that first arrive together are not arbitrarily selected. Missing IDs,
invalid arrival labels and rejected/unmatched events remain visible.

Admission checks supplied event type, immutable ID, original request/claim,
directory Finance actor/payee, EUR currency, UTC business time, reason and event
shape. Settlements/refunds must already be positive integer cents: Finance events
are never rounded. Accepted, adjustment and resolution targets must be known
nonnegative integer cents. Status events with blank amounts have no monetary
effect; blanks do not become confirmed zero payments.

Events are consumed by arrival batch. Business time and reference dependencies
order effects within each batch; source row order is not authority. Missing
acceptance/original-transfer references are retried when evidence arrives.
Earlier batch views remain unchanged when a later batch resolves a reference.
Accepted-target effects use business chronology, so a late earlier adjustment
does not revive a subsequently cancelled request. Equal-time conflicting targets
remain unresolved. No new acceptance ID can create a duplicate commitment for
the same request.

A refund needs an admitted settled original transfer on the same request, claim,
payee and currency; it must occur later and cannot exceed that transfer's
unrecovered amount. Promises and request/status events never reduce net paid.
Competing equal-time refunds exceeding the original transfer are all held rather
than selected by identifier spelling. Failed attempts have no monetary effect;
retry authority remains distinct. A reported settled transfer is retained even
when retry authority is missing, with a hold identifying that authorization gap.

Finance cancellation releases the accepted request target to zero while retaining
the original accepted amount and every transfer/refund. This is request accounting,
not zero employee entitlement. A late transfer is still admitted to the original
request and creates a Finance reconciliation issue. A resolution records Finance's
supplied request-level target; it does not itself change a commitment. Its target,
current accepted target and known net must agree. Later-observed money reopens
the assessment even if a previous resolution exists.

## Amount and attribution semantics

Claims and every expense occurrence retain gross original-currency amounts,
base caps/allowed amounts from validation, policy-allowed amounts, and eligibility
status. Converted gross and policy arithmetic use line rounding already specified
by policy. Request amounts are separate:

- `original_accepted_cents`: immutable first accepted amount.
- `accepted_cents`: current request target after admitted adjustment/cancellation.
- `admitted_settled_cents`, `admitted_refund_cents`, `admitted_net_cents`: the exact
  sum of admitted retained facts, counting each business event once.
- `net_confirmed_settled_cents`: known request-level net when settlement evidence
  exists and no delivery uncertainty remains; otherwise null. Admitted subtotals
  remain visible when exact net is unknown.
- `accepted_minus_net_cents`: a request-level comparison, not a current authorized
  claim balance. A negative value requires Finance attention.

Finance explicitly supplies request and claim references, but **no claim-revision
or expense columns**. The validator retains candidates as of original acceptance,
including the available revisions, current candidate trip/costs, and supplied
reviews available by the acceptance's business instant. These are transparent
derived candidates, not certified attribution. Revision/expense accepted and net
amounts remain null, and no payment authority is inferred from equal amounts.

C03/C24's same employee/trip/cost/receipt/currency/gross identity links the repeated
purchase. If the earlier candidate bundle is fully settled, a conditional excluded
amount and incremental policy calculation are shown. Partial settlements are
never allocated among costs by guess. The conditional calculation does not create
a new obligation or authorize payment: explicit request/cost allocation remains
an owned unresolved item.

Policy validation is recomputed for each selected batch and at original acceptance
with later business-time reviews/cancellations filtered out. Original acceptance
does not turn a historical approval into current authority. Current role decisions,
packet identity, cancellation context and all increment 3 evidence gaps still
govern further payment readiness. The artifact retains the 18 normalization
diagnostics and current policy/review diagnostics.

Decision 001 creates a blocked hold when a correction follows an already observed
original acceptance. It requires Finance resolution of the original-request
consequences and valid current reviews. A request-only resolution does not prove
its scope covers the current revision/cost/cancellation. C18/r2 remains blocked;

authorization.

C09's first acceptance is in its corrected revision's arrival batch, so no earlier
accepted original request is invented. C121's permit-only business cancellation

                bad.append('Reviewed estimate (EUR)')
            if 'budget_owner' in roles and (not expected_budget or set(p.get('Budget record references') or []) != expected_budget):
                bad.append('Budget record references')
            if 'director' in roles and not p.get('Budget owner position'):
                bad.append('Budget owner position')
            for cancel in cancel_context:
                if cancel['cancellation_id'] not in (p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) or not time or time <= instant(cancel['confirmed_at']):
                    bad.append('Travel cancellation references/post-confirmation time')
            # References to an unrelated or unconfirmed cancellation cannot establish context.
            if set(p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) != {c['cancellation_id'] for c in cancel_context}:
                bad.append('Travel cancellation references')
            add('review_packet', 'blocked' if bad else 'supported',
                'Packet differs from current evidence: ' + ', '.join(sorted(set(bad))) if bad else 'Packet matches exact current subject evidence and role context.', 'freshness')
        outcome = v.get('Outcome')
        if outcome not in ('approve', 'return', 'reject') or not v.get('Reason') or (outcome == 'return' and not v.get('Repair requested')):
            add('review_outcome', 'unresolved', 'Outcome needs an explicit reason and a concrete repair request for return.')
        usable = status(fs) == 'supported'
        entry = {'decision_id': v.get('Decision reference'), 'record_id': row['record_id'],
                 'revision': v.get('Revision'), 'outcome': outcome, 'roles': roles,
                 'source_revisions': versions,
                 'decision_time': v.get('Decision time (UTC)'), 'status': status(fs), 'findings': fs}
        imports.append(entry)
        if usable:
            for role in roles:
                candidates[role].append(entry)
    findings, selections = [], {}
    for role in required:
        items = candidates[role]
        latest_time = max((e['decision_time'] for e in items), default=None)
        latest = [e for e in items if e['decision_time'] == latest_time]
        chosen = unique(latest)
        if chosen:
            selections[role] = chosen['decision_id']
            state = 'supported' if chosen['outcome'] == 'approve' else 'blocked'
            reason = 'Supplied current approve response.' if state == 'supported' else 'Supplied ' + chosen['outcome'] + ' response; retain reason/repair in bound ledger.'
            refs = [chosen['record_id']]
        else:
            state, reason, refs = 'unresolved', 'Missing or ambiguous valid current response; old revisions and invalid packets satisfy no role.', [r['record_id'] for r in relevant]
        findings.append(finding('review_' + role, state, reason, refs + [claim['record_id'], person['record_id']], 'roles', pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) or 'Administration'))
    if amount is None:
        findings.append(finding('director_threshold', 'unresolved', 'Reviewed amount unknown: director requirement cannot be determined.', [claim['record_id']], 'roles', pv['Director']))
    if subject_type == 'claim':
        findings.append(finding('reviewed_entitlement_binding', 'unresolved', 'Packets have no reviewed claim entitlement field or exception-reference field; amount/exception seen by reviewers cannot be independently matched.', [e['record_id'] for e in imports] + [claim['record_id']], 'freshness'))
    return {'subject_type': subject_type, 'subject_id': subject, 'revision': revision,
            'required_roles': required, 'selected_decisions': selections, 'findings': findings,
            'imports': imports, 'status': status(findings)}

| Alternative | Defensible use and limitation | Selection |

The benefit is earlier independent verification and repair preparation without permitting stale evidence to authorize downstream work. ## Operational interpretation and restrictions

1. Identify the missing or changed fact, source version, affected subject/revision, and operation whose basis depends on it. 4. If dependency scope is uncertain, retain an owned unresolved scope item and the necessary conservative hold. Establish independence before releasing affected work; absence of a recorded edge alone is insufficient when a shared source, ledger, or obligation may govern it. Do not invent a connection or declare a universal dependency without explaining the uncertainty.
5. Preserve gross purchase amounts, policy-calculated amounts, reviewed entitlement, Finance request facts, and attributed settlement separately. Missing evidence is unknown, not zero or paid. Continue observing original requests, late transfers, cancellations, refunds, and conflicts while held.
6. This decision grants no approval, exception, permit, Finance resolution, dispatch, booking, payment, or closure authority. It waives no review, receipt, merchant-payment proof, or cancellation-aware review requirement. It clears no existing repair item. Owners remain those evidenced by the directory/policy and existing queue; questions of rule or scope go to the lead/facilitator, financial attribution/resolution to authorized Finance, and missing employee evidence to its evidenced owner. ## Alternatives and rationale

| Approach | Benefit | Limitation and decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim/revision-first | Strong local accountability and straightforward revision history. | Repeats common package/evidence requests and may obscure one shared root. Retain as a case view, not the sole organizing identity. |
| Owner-first | Useful for handoff, workload, and collecting one person's outstanding evidence. | One owner may have unrelated facts and cases; owner changes must not merge requirements or erase history. Retain as an optional derived view, not the primary blocker identity. |
| Shared blocker plus linked case views | One central missing fact/definition and accountable owner, with evidence-backed impact links and independent case requirements. | Selected. Requires explicit scope, stable identities, bidirectional traceability, and careful partial-response/recheck handling. |

The selected approach reduces duplicate repair coordination while retaining the exact case/revision requirements needed for safe resumption. Grouping by similar wording, diagnostic code, actor, amount, or batch alone cannot establish that two items share a blocker. The central repair owner coordinates provision/clarification of that fact; ownership does not grant approval, exception, payment, or cancellation authority.

## Restrictions and intended implementation consequences

1. A future central blocker must retain a stable identity, exact missing fact or conflict, accountable evidence/rule owner, current state, source/version references, required evidence/next action, applicability scope, and run/batch lifecycle history. If ownership or scope is unknown, record that uncertainty and its clarification step; do not invent a named actor or global case linkage.
2. Affected-case links must identify claim and revision, relevant expense/trip/permit/request where applicable, the case repair identity, dependency/path evidence, and the operation held. Support central-to-case and case-to-central navigation. Unknown applicability is explicitly unresolved; do not manufacture proven graph edges to populate a view.
3. Every observed claim/revision retains its local requirements and history, including superseded versions. A case with no active repair can show that fact without creating one. Requests and cancellation processes without claims remain visible without fabricated claim rows.
4. Keep central fact state, link/recheck state, local repair state, and financial closure distinct. New shared evidence triggers only evidenced dependent rechecks under Decision 002. Each local requirement needs its own supported disposition; a blocker becoming resolved is never a blanket case-clear operation. A case may legitimately remain held after its shared blocker is resolved.
5. Record partial responses against the exact fact/scope they establish. Conflicting, stale, wrong-role, wrong-subject, or wrong-revision replies remain visible and unresolved for applicable authorization. Preserve raw replies and prior versions; unchanged totals do not excuse current reviews.
6. Preserve all case-specific merchant-proof, approval, Finance allocation/resolution, and Decision 001 holds. No approval, permit, refund, payment proof, financial authority, paid status, or closure can be inferred from grouping or ownership. Gross purchase, allowed arithmetic, request facts, and attributed settlement remain separate.
7. Version the central register and derived views in a new output directory with source hashes, decision binding, predecessor/run links, and repair-history migration mappings. Earlier repair IDs and states remain traceable. Do not retroactively add Decision 003 to existing manifests or clear the earlier register by migration.

## Finding semantics

`supported` means the stated rule is established by the referenced evidence.
`blocked` means an observed rule failure, supplied return/rejection, or an explicit
hold. `unresolved` means missing, ambiguous or unverifiable evidence/definitions.
Every finding records a rule, reason, owner, source references and required repair.
The source index resolves record IDs to source hashes and PDF pages or workbook
sheet/rows. Rule references resolve to policy lines. The original 18 normalization
diagnostics are preserved globally and attached to their claim revisions.

Gross purchase, base capped amount, explicit replacement allowed amount and
converted cents are separate fields. Unknown paid evidence, category, cap or FX
never becomes zero. Personal purchases have known zero entitlement. Monetary
outputs in EUR are integer cents; original-currency decimals remain strings.
Each converted line is rounded decimal half-up before summing. Calculated totals
are gross policy calculations, **not authorized or incrementally payable amounts**.
Shared costs such as C03/C24 retain both occurrences and an owned unresolved
prior-obligation link; exclusion requires the deferred Finance stage.

`eligibility_status` aggregates expense eligibility and identity/date checks.
`approval_status` covers supplied current role responses and packet limitations.
Overall claim `status` also includes historical arrangement failures and original
request holds. `current_at_batch` distinguishes current from historical revisions.
All revisions are rechecked against the selected batch's visible facts; these are
not execution-time snapshots of earlier batches. Global unresolved findings apply
even where individual eligibility or role checks are supported.

Corrections use a full dependency recheck, allowed by policy line 23 and the
stakeholder interview. No claim review is inherited from another revision, even
when totals match. Exact claim and permit subjects/revisions are independent.
Packets must match employee, trip/permit revisions, expense IDs, policy and business
context. Role authority comes from the employee's directory row. Only the joint
budget-owner/supervisor response may cover two roles. Director thresholds use
strictly more than EUR 1,000: trip estimate for permit, calculated entitlement for
claim. Missing entitlement leaves the director requirement unresolved.

Visible valid replies are ordered by business decision time for each role; an
equal-time ambiguity is held. Returns require a concrete repair request; rejects
retain their reason. Invalid, stale and wrong-role imports remain visible and
satisfy no required role. Rejection here does not close a claim or erase money.

Cancellation deliveries are checked for immutable payload conflicts, unique
initiation/confirmation, exact trip/permit targets, directory employee/supervisor
authority, arrival visibility, strictly later confirmation, and own-time effect.
All four observed processes, including no-claim TC122, remain separate. A permit
cancellation leaves its trip active; an old trip cancellation does not affect a
replacement trip. Timely historical permission is retained after cancellation.
Spent costs need an exact `travel_cancellation` Finance exception plus fresh,
post-confirmation cancellation-aware packets. An amount-only exception does not
cover it. Exceptions never approve arrangements or supply payment evidence.

The supplied Budget ledger context subtracts net settled expenditure and only the
unsettled portion of commitments, avoiding double subtraction. Packets must name
the entire supplied department/project/period ledger. Accepted new Finance
requests remain outside this calculation, so budget completeness is unresolved.
Adequate funds do not substitute for a budget-owner response.

values, decoded raw cells and source locators. Finance event IDs form a separate
namespace from business cancellation activity IDs. Immutable Finance payloads
compare all decoded raw fields and normalized values except arrival batch.

An exact redelivery has no additional monetary or commitment effect. A later
conflicting payload cannot replace the earlier admitted event or erase its money;
all affected requests are held and exact net becomes unresolved. Conflicting
payloads that first arrive together are not arbitrarily selected. Missing IDs,

request and creates a Finance reconciliation issue. A resolution records Finance's

- `net_confirmed_settled_cents`: known request-level net when settlement evidence
  exists and no delivery uncertainty remains; otherwise null. Admitted subtotals

- `accepted_minus_net_cents`: a request-level comparison, not a current authorized
  claim balance. A negative value requires Finance attention.

            add('review_outcome', 'unresolved', 'Outcome needs an explicit reason and a concrete repair request for return.')
        usable = status(fs) == 'supported'
        entry = {'decision_id': v.get('Decision reference'), 'record_id': row['record_id'],
                 'revision': v.get('Revision'), 'outcome': outcome, 'roles': roles,
                 'source_revisions': versions,
                 'decision_time': v.get('Decision time (UTC)'), 'status': status(fs), 'findings': fs}
        imports.append(entry)
        if usable:
            for role in roles:
                candidates[role].append(entry)
    findings, selections = [], {}
    for role in required:
        items = candidates[role]
        latest_time = max((e['decision_time'] for e in items), default=None)
        latest = [e for e in items if e['decision_time'] == latest_time]
        chosen = unique(latest)
        if chosen:
            selections[role] = chosen['decision_id']
            state = 'supported' if chosen['outcome'] == 'approve' else 'blocked'
            reason = 'Supplied current approve response.' if state == 'supported' else 'Supplied ' + chosen['outcome'] + ' response; retain reason/repair in bound ledger.'
            refs = [chosen['record_id']]
        else:
            state, reason, refs = 'unresolved', 'Missing or ambiguous valid current response; old revisions and invalid packets satisfy no role.', [r['record_id'] for r in relevant]
        findings.append(finding('review_' + role, state, reason, refs + [claim['record_id'], person['record_id']], 'roles', pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) or 'Administration'))
    if amount is None:
        findings.append(finding('director_threshold', 'unresolved', 'Reviewed amount unknown: director requirement cannot be determined.', [claim['record_id']], 'roles', pv['Director']))
    if subject_type == 'claim':
        findings.append(finding('reviewed_entitlement_binding', 'unresolved', 'Packets have no reviewed claim entitlement field or exception-reference field; amount/exception seen by reviewers cannot be independently matched.', [e['record_id'] for e in imports] + [claim['record_id']], 'freshness'))
    return {'subject_type': subject_type, 'subject_id': subject, 'revision': revision,
            'required_roles': required, 'selected_decisions': selections, 'findings': findings,
            'imports': imports, 'status': status(findings)}

    tv, pv = trip['values'], person['values']
    subject = claim['claim_id'] if subject_type == 'claim' else tv['Permit reference']
    revision = claim['revision'] if subject_type == 'claim' else tv['Permit revision']
    required = ['administration', 'budget_owner', 'supervisor']
    if amount is not None and amount > Decimal('1000'):
        required.append('director')
    relevant = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review ledger') if visible(r, batch)
                and r['values'].get('Subject type') == subject_type and r['values'].get('Subject reference') == subject]
    imports, candidates = [], defaultdict(list)
    scoped_budget = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Budget') if all(r['values'].get(k) == pv.get(k) for k in ('Department', 'Project', 'Budget period'))]
    expected_budget = {r['values']['Ledger reference'] for r in scoped_budget}
    for row in relevant:
        v, fs = row['values'], []
        refs = [row['record_id'], trip['record_id'], person['record_id']]
        def add(code, state, reason, rule='roles', more=()):
            fs.append(finding(code, state, reason, refs + list(more), rule, v.get('Reviewer') or 'Administration'))
        if v.get('Revision') != revision:
            add('review_revision', 'blocked', 'Historical revision cannot authorize this subject/version.', 'freshness')
        if subject_type == 'claim' and v.get('Arrival batch', 0) < claim['arrival_batch']:
            add('review_arrival', 'blocked', 'Reply arrived before this claim revision.', 'freshness')
        roles = v.get('Review roles') or []
        role_ok = (bool(roles) and len(set(roles)) == len(roles)
                   and all(role in ROLE_FIELDS and pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) == v.get('Reviewer') for role in roles)
                   and (len(roles) == 1 or set(roles) == {'budget_owner', 'supervisor'}))
        add('review_authority', 'supported' if role_ok else 'blocked',
            'Only directory actors may fill their roles; only budget owner/supervisor may share a response.')
        time = instant(v.get('Decision time (UTC)'))
        if time is None or time.astimezone(ZONE).date() > CASE_DATE:
            add('review_time', 'unresolved', 'Decision time missing, non-UTC or future.', 'clock')
        versions = v.get('Source revisions') or []
        if not {'POL-2026.2', 'SRC-D-3'}.issubset(versions) or any(t.startswith('POL-') and t != 'POL-2026.2' for t in versions) or any(t.startswith('SRC-') and t != 'SRC-D-3' for t in versions):
            add('review_sources', 'blocked', 'Policy or retained business-source revision is missing or stale.', 'freshness')
        else:
            add('review_sources', 'supported', 'Policy and printed source revision match retained text; opaque package tokens remain a global unresolved definition.', 'freshness')
        duplicates = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review ledger') if visible(r, batch) and r['values'].get('Decision reference') == v.get('Decision reference')]
        if len(duplicates) != 1:
            add('review_identity', 'unresolved', 'Decision reference is not unique; no silent selection.', 'freshness')
        packets = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review packets') if r['values'].get('Decision reference') == v.get('Decision reference')]
        packet = unique(packets)
        if not packet:
            add('review_packet', 'unresolved', 'Exactly one bound review packet is required.', more=[r['record_id'] for r in packets])
        else:
            p = packet['values']; refs.append(packet['record_id'])
            expected = {'Employee ID': claim['employee_id'], 'Trip reference': claim['trip_id'],
                        'Trip revision': claim['trip_revision'], 'Permit reference': tv['Permit reference'],
                        'Permit revision': tv['Permit revision'], 'Policy revision': 'POL-2026.2'}
            bad = [k for k, value in expected.items() if p.get(k) != value]
            for field in ('Business purpose', 'Client', 'Schedule coverage', 'Alternatives considered'):
                if p.get(field) != tv.get(field) or not p.get(field):

            if subject_type == 'claim' and set(p.get('Expense references') or []) != {e['expense_id'] for e in claim['expenses']}:
                bad.append('Expense references')
            if subject_type == 'permit' and number(p.get('Reviewed estimate (EUR)')) != number(tv.get('Estimate (EUR)')):
                bad.append('Reviewed estimate (EUR)')
            if 'budget_owner' in roles and (not expected_budget or set(p.get('Budget record references') or []) != expected_budget):
                bad.append('Budget record references')
            if 'director' in roles and not p.get('Budget owner position'):
                bad.append('Budget owner position')
            for cancel in cancel_context:
                if cancel['cancellation_id'] not in (p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) or not time or time <= instant(cancel['confirmed_at']):
                    bad.append('Travel cancellation references/post-confirmation time')
            # References to an unrelated or unconfirmed cancellation cannot establish context.
            if set(p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) != {c['cancellation_id'] for c in cancel_context}:
                bad.append('Travel cancellation references')
            add('review_packet', 'blocked' if bad else 'supported',
                'Packet differs from current evidence: ' + ', '.join(sorted(set(bad))) if bad else 'Packet matches exact current subject evidence and role context.', 'freshness')
        outcome = v.get('Outcome')
        if outcome not in ('approve', 'return', 'reject') or not v.get('Reason') or (outcome == 'return' and not v.get('Repair requested')):
            add('review_outcome', 'unresolved', 'Outcome needs an explicit reason and a concrete repair request for return.')
        usable = status(fs) == 'supported'
        entry = {'decision_id': v.get('Decision reference'), 'record_id': row['record_id'],
                 'revision': v.get('Revision'), 'outcome': outcome, 'roles': roles,
                 'source_revisions': versions,
                 'decision_time': v.get('Decision time (UTC)'), 'status': status(fs), 'findings': fs}
        imports.append(entry)
        if usable:
            for role in roles:
                candidates[role].append(entry)
    findings, selections = [], {}
    for role in required:
        items = candidates[role]
        latest_time = max((e['decision_time'] for e in items), default=None)
        latest = [e for e in items if e['decision_time'] == latest_time]
        chosen = unique(latest)
        if chosen:
            selections[role] = chosen['decision_id']
            state = 'supported' if chosen['outcome'] == 'approve' else 'blocked'
            reason = 'Supplied current approve response.' if state == 'supported' else 'Supplied ' + chosen['outcome'] + ' response; retain reason/repair in bound ledger.'
            refs = [chosen['record_id']]
        else:
            state, reason, refs = 'unresolved', 'Missing or ambiguous valid current response; old revisions and invalid packets satisfy no role.', [r['record_id'] for r in relevant]
        findings.append(finding('review_' + role, state, reason, refs + [claim['record_id'], person['record_id']], 'roles', pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) or 'Administration'))
    if amount is None:
        findings.append(finding('director_threshold', 'unresolved', 'Reviewed amount unknown: director requirement cannot be determined.', [claim['record_id']], 'roles', pv['Director']))
    if subject_type == 'claim':

    return {'subject_type': subject_type, 'subject_id': subject, 'revision': revision,
            'required_roles': required, 'selected_decisions': selections, 'findings': findings,
            'imports': imports, 'status': status(findings)}

## Alternatives considered and rationale

| Alternative | Defensible use and limitation | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim-level isolation | Simple ownership and continued work on other claims. Sufficient when the evidence establishes no relevant cross-claim dependencies; insufficient when claims reuse one purchase or share a budget/obligation basis. | Not the general rule. |
| Whole-batch containment | Conservative when an inaccessible source, corrupt input, or shared definition genuinely prevents establishing independence. Delays unrelated verification and repair preparation; an arrival batch alone is not evidence that all work is dependent. | Not the default. Retain a wider hold when its scope cannot yet be established, with an owned explanation. |
| Dependency-based containment | Holds affected checks and downstream work, including links across claims, while permitting unrelated evidence work. Requires traceable scope and explicit handling of uncertain dependencies. | Authorized selection. |

The benefit is earlier independent verification and repair preparation without permitting stale evidence to authorize downstream work. The cost is maintaining evidence-backed dependency scope and explaining uncertainty. A common employee, equal amount, neighboring spreadsheet row, or common arrival batch alone does not prove the relevant dependency. Conversely, different claim IDs do not prove independence.

## Operational interpretation and restrictions

1. Identify the missing or changed fact, source version, affected subject/revision, and operation whose basis depends on it. Follow proven dependency paths into expense findings, review packets/decisions, travel authority, requests, or reconciliation. Record direction, source references, reason, and scope; do not turn a possible association into certified financial attribution.
2. Hold the affected operation and its dependent authorization/readiness. Continue independent evidence acquisition where otherwise authorized, parsing, arithmetic, verification, and preparation with honest partial/unresolved labels. A held payment process may still accumulate verified evidence and preserve incoming Finance facts.
3. Recheck material corrections even if money totals match. A dependency-limited recheck requires justification for what remains valid; use a full affected-subject recheck when independence is not established. Historical approvals remain history. No stale approval becomes current because an unrelated check passed.
4. If dependency scope is uncertain, retain an owned unresolved scope item and the necessary conservative hold. Establish independence before releasing affected work; absence of a recorded edge alone is insufficient when a shared source, ledger, or obligation may govern it. Do not invent a connection or declare a universal dependency without explaining the uncertainty.
5. Preserve gross purchase amounts, policy-calculated amounts, reviewed entitlement, Finance request facts, and attributed settlement separately. Missing evidence is unknown, not zero or paid. Continue observing original requests, late transfers, cancellations, refunds, and conflicts while held.
6. This decision grants no approval, exception, permit, Finance resolution, dispatch, booking, payment, or closure authority. It waives no review, receipt, merchant-payment proof, or cancellation-aware review requirement. It clears no existing repair item. Owners remain those evidenced by the directory/policy and existing queue; questions of rule or scope go to the lead/facilitator, financial attribution/resolution to authorized Finance, and missing employee evidence to its evidenced owner. No request is sent by this record.
7. Preserve arrival order, source hashes, rejected imports, immutable event identities, previous snapshots, and repair history. Later implementation must bind this decision in new versioned outputs. Do not add it retroactively to existing manifests or rewrite earlier evidence.

Before admission, verification rechecks acquisition identities, source hashes and
lengths, supplemental policy/provenance, and the complete normalized records and
parsing report against an in-memory parse. It verifies every increment 3 input
binding, the full recomputed validation content, and its summary. Missing governing
bindings, corrupt records, changed code, or tampered summaries fail verification.
Output bindings include the verified validation artifact and reconciliation code.
The case clock remains November 15, 2026, Europe/Amsterdam, from preserved policy
line 11; machine time does not affect execution.

## Admission and replay

All deliveries visible at the selected arrival horizon retain their normalized
values, decoded raw cells and source locators. Finance event IDs form a separate
namespace from business cancellation activity IDs. Immutable Finance payloads
compare all decoded raw fields and normalized values except arrival batch.

An exact redelivery has no additional monetary or commitment effect. A later
conflicting payload cannot replace the earlier admitted event or erase its money;
all affected requests are held and exact net becomes unresolved. Conflicting
payloads that first arrive together are not arbitrarily selected. Missing IDs,
invalid arrival labels and rejected/unmatched events remain visible.

Admission checks supplied event type, immutable ID, original request/claim,
directory Finance actor/payee, EUR currency, UTC business time, reason and event
shape. Settlements/refunds must already be positive integer cents: Finance events
are never rounded. Accepted, adjustment and resolution targets must be known
nonnegative integer cents. Status events with blank amounts have no monetary
effect; blanks do not become confirmed zero payments.

Events are consumed by arrival batch. Business time and reference dependencies
order effects within each batch; source row order is not authority. Missing
acceptance/original-transfer references are retried when evidence arrives.
Earlier batch views remain unchanged when a later batch resolves a reference.
Accepted-target effects use business chronology, so a late earlier adjustment
does not revive a subsequently cancelled request. Equal-time conflicting targets
remain unresolved. No new acceptance ID can create a duplicate commitment for
the same request.

A refund needs an admitted settled original transfer on the same request, claim,
payee and currency; it must occur later and cannot exceed that transfer's
unrecovered amount. Promises and request/status events never reduce net paid.
Competing equal-time refunds exceeding the original transfer are all held rather
than selected by identifier spelling. Failed attempts have no monetary effect;
retry authority remains distinct. A reported settled transfer is retained even
when retry authority is missing, with a hold identifying that authorization gap.

Finance cancellation releases the accepted request target to zero while retaining
the original accepted amount and every transfer/refund. This is request accounting,
not zero employee entitlement. A late transfer is still admitted to the original
request and creates a Finance reconciliation issue. A resolution records Finance's
supplied request-level target; it does not itself change a commitment. Its target,
current accepted target and known net must agree. Later-observed money reopens
the assessment even if a previous resolution exists.

## Amount and attribution semantics

Claims and every expense occurrence retain gross original-currency amounts,
base caps/allowed amounts from validation, policy-allowed amounts, and eligibility
status. Converted gross and policy arithmetic use line rounding already specified
by policy. Request amounts are separate:

- `original_accepted_cents`: immutable first accepted amount.
- `accepted_cents`: current request target after admitted adjustment/cancellation.
- `admitted_settled_cents`, `admitted_refund_cents`, `admitted_net_cents`: the exact
  sum of admitted retained facts, counting each business event once.
- `net_confirmed_settled_cents`: known request-level net when settlement evidence
  exists and no delivery uncertainty remains; otherwise null. Admitted subtotals
  remain visible when exact net is unknown.
- `accepted_minus_net_cents`: a request-level comparison, not a current authorized
  claim balance. A negative value requires Finance attention.

Finance explicitly supplies request and claim references, but **no claim-revision
or expense columns**. The validator retains candidates as of original acceptance,
including the available revisions, current candidate trip/costs, and supplied
reviews available by the acceptance's business instant. These are transparent
derived candidates, not certified attribution. Revision/expense accepted and net
amounts remain null, and no payment authority is inferred from equal amounts.

C03/C24's same employee/trip/cost/receipt/currency/gross identity links the repeated
purchase. If the earlier candidate bundle is fully settled, a conditional excluded
amount and incremental policy calculation are shown. Partial settlements are
never allocated among costs by guess. The conditional calculation does not create
a new obligation or authorize payment: explicit request/cost allocation remains
an owned unresolved item.

## Freshness, cancellation and Decision 001

Policy validation is recomputed for each selected batch and at original acceptance
with later business-time reviews/cancellations filtered out. Original acceptance
does not turn a historical approval into current authority. Current role decisions,
packet identity, cancellation context and all increment 3 evidence gaps still
govern further payment readiness. The artifact retains the 18 normalization
diagnostics and current policy/review diagnostics.

Decision 001 creates a blocked hold when a correction follows an already observed
original acceptance. It requires Finance resolution of the original-request
consequences and valid current reviews. A request-only resolution does not prove
its scope covers the current revision/cost/cancellation. C18/r2 remains blocked;
its original EUR 100 late transfer is not attributed to COST-18B. C19's request-level
EUR 80 agreement and supplied resolution remain separate from current claim
authorization.

C09's first acceptance is in its corrected revision's arrival batch, so no earlier
accepted original request is invented. C121's permit-only business cancellation
precedes its first observed acceptance; it does not automatically require a
separate post-acceptance Finance resolution. Its trip remains active and its permit
retired. Cancellation confirmation on T18 never targets T18B. All four business
processes remain separate, including TC122 with no observed claim/request. Business
cancellation itself changes no Finance money or accepted commitment.

## Limits and handoff

The artifact is partial. Finance owns uncertain request/revision/cost allocation,
missing or conflicting events, refunds and resolution scope. Reviewers own valid
current decisions and missing packet amount/exception evidence. The facilitator
owns the undefined independent `DW-D-2` binding and native source completeness.
The preserved browser policy's provenance limitations remain applicable; there is
no fresh-source acquisition claim or independent bank completeness assertion.

All factual amounts can be reconciled at request level without certifying that
the corresponding claim was authorized. Inherited unknown categories, missing
merchant payment proof, missing rates/caps and reviewed-entitlement/exception
packet fields are never waived by Finance acceptance or equal net amounts.
The historical assignment-access limitation remains visible in validation.

No new payment-ready state, request draft, final `claims.csv`, `report.md`, Skill,
submission output, financial closure or public snapshot-schema state is emitted.
`batch_views` are internal replay evidence, not final submission snapshots. Keep
this stage separate from later authority repair, closure and delivery increments.

def review(doc, claim, trip, person, batch, subject_type, amount, cancel_context=()):
    """Validate supplied decisions and packets; never supply discretionary judgment."""
    tv, pv = trip['values'], person['values']
    subject = claim['claim_id'] if subject_type == 'claim' else tv['Permit reference']
    revision = claim['revision'] if subject_type == 'claim' else tv['Permit revision']
    required = ['administration', 'budget_owner', 'supervisor']
    if amount is not None and amount > Decimal('1000'):
        required.append('director')
    relevant = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review ledger') if visible(r, batch)
                and r['values'].get('Subject type') == subject_type and r['values'].get('Subject reference') == subject]
    imports, candidates = [], defaultdict(list)
    scoped_budget = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Budget') if all(r['values'].get(k) == pv.get(k) for k in ('Department', 'Project', 'Budget period'))]
    expected_budget = {r['values']['Ledger reference'] for r in scoped_budget}
    for row in relevant:
        v, fs = row['values'], []
        refs = [row['record_id'], trip['record_id'], person['record_id']]
        def add(code, state, reason, rule='roles', more=()):
            fs.append(finding(code, state, reason, refs + list(more), rule, v.get('Reviewer') or 'Administration'))
        if v.get('Revision') != revision:
            add('review_revision', 'blocked', 'Historical revision cannot authorize this subject/version.', 'freshness')
        if subject_type == 'claim' and v.get('Arrival batch', 0) < claim['arrival_batch']:
            add('review_arrival', 'blocked', 'Reply arrived before this claim revision.', 'freshness')
        roles = v.get('Review roles') or []
        role_ok = (bool(roles) and len(set(roles)) == len(roles)
                   and all(role in ROLE_FIELDS and pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) == v.get('Reviewer') for role in roles)
                   and (len(roles) == 1 or set(roles) == {'budget_owner', 'supervisor'}))
        add('review_authority', 'supported' if role_ok else 'blocked',
            'Only directory actors may fill their roles; only budget owner/supervisor may share a response.')
        time = instant(v.get('Decision time (UTC)'))
        if time is None or time.astimezone(ZONE).date() > CASE_DATE:
            add('review_time', 'unresolved', 'Decision time missing, non-UTC or future.', 'clock')
        versions = v.get('Source revisions') or []
        if not {'POL-2026.2', 'SRC-D-3'}.issubset(versions) or any(t.startswith('POL-') and t != 'POL-2026.2' for t in versions) or any(t.startswith('SRC-') and t != 'SRC-D-3' for t in versions):
            add('review_sources', 'blocked', 'Policy or retained business-source revision is missing or stale.', 'freshness')
        else:
            add('review_sources', 'supported', 'Policy and printed source revision match retained text; opaque package tokens remain a global unresolved definition.', 'freshness')
        duplicates = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review ledger') if visible(r, batch) and r['values'].get('Decision reference') == v.get('Decision reference')]
        if len(duplicates) != 1:
            add('review_identity', 'unresolved', 'Decision reference is not unique; no silent selection.', 'freshness')
        packets = [r for r in rows(doc, 'Review packets') if r['values'].get('Decision reference') == v.get('Decision reference')]
        packet = unique(packets)
        if not packet:
            add('review_packet', 'unresolved', 'Exactly one bound review packet is required.', more=[r['record_id'] for r in packets])
        else:
            p = packet['values']; refs.append(packet['record_id'])
            expected = {'Employee ID': claim['employee_id'], 'Trip reference': claim['trip_id'],
                        'Trip revision': claim['trip_revision'], 'Permit reference': tv['Permit reference'],
                        'Permit revision': tv['Permit revision'], 'Policy revision': 'POL-2026.2'}
            bad = [k for k, value in expected.items() if p.get(k) != value]
            for field in ('Business purpose', 'Client', 'Schedule coverage', 'Alternatives considered'):
                if p.get(field) != tv.get(field) or not p.get(field):
                    bad.append(field)
            if subject_type == 'claim' and set(p.get('Expense references') or []) != {e['expense_id'] for e in claim['expenses']}:
                bad.append('Expense references')
            if subject_type == 'permit' and number(p.get('Reviewed estimate (EUR)')) != number(tv.get('Estimate (EUR)')):
                bad.append('Reviewed estimate (EUR)')
            if 'budget_owner' in roles and (not expected_budget or set(p.get('Budget record references') or []) != expected_budget):
                bad.append('Budget record references')
            if 'director' in roles and not p.get('Budget owner position'):
                bad.append('Budget owner position')
            for cancel in cancel_context:
                if cancel['cancellation_id'] not in (p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) or not time or time <= instant(cancel['confirmed_at']):
                    bad.append('Travel cancellation references/post-confirmation time')
            # References to an unrelated or unconfirmed cancellation cannot establish context.
            if set(p.get('Travel cancellation references') or []) != {c['cancellation_id'] for c in cancel_context}:
                bad.append('Travel cancellation references')
            add('review_packet', 'blocked' if bad else 'supported',
                'Packet differs from current evidence: ' + ', '.join(sorted(set(bad))) if bad else 'Packet matches exact current subject evidence and role context.', 'freshness')
        outcome = v.get('Outcome')
        if outcome not in ('approve', 'return', 'reject') or not v.get('Reason') or (outcome == 'return' and not v.get('Repair requested')):
            add('review_outcome', 'unresolved', 'Outcome needs an explicit reason and a concrete repair request for return.')
        usable = status(fs) == 'supported'
        entry = {'decision_id': v.get('Decision reference'), 'record_id': row['record_id'],
                 'revision': v.get('Revision'), 'outcome': outcome, 'roles': roles,
                 'source_revisions': versions,
                 'decision_time': v.get('Decision time (UTC)'), 'status': status(fs), 'findings': fs}
        imports.append(entry)
        if usable:
            for role in roles:
                candidates[role].append(entry)
    findings, selections = [], {}
    for role in required:
        items = candidates[role]
        latest_time = max((e['decision_time'] for e in items), default=None)
        latest = [e for e in items if e['decision_time'] == latest_time]
        chosen = unique(latest)
        if chosen:
            selections[role] = chosen['decision_id']
            state = 'supported' if chosen['outcome'] == 'approve' else 'blocked'
            reason = 'Supplied current approve response.' if state == 'supported' else 'Supplied ' + chosen['outcome'] + ' response; retain reason/repair in bound ledger.'
            refs = [chosen['record_id']]
        else:
            state, reason, refs = 'unresolved', 'Missing or ambiguous valid current response; old revisions and invalid packets satisfy no role.', [r['record_id'] for r in relevant]
        findings.append(finding('review_' + role, state, reason, refs + [claim['record_id'], person['record_id']], 'roles', pv.get(ROLE_FIELDS[role]) or 'Administration'))
    if amount is None:
        findings.append(finding('director_threshold', 'unresolved', 'Reviewed amount unknown: director requirement cannot be determined.', [claim['record_id']], 'roles', pv['Director']))
    if subject_type == 'claim':
        findings.append(finding('reviewed_entitlement_binding', 'unresolved', 'Packets have no reviewed claim entitlement field or exception-reference field; amount/exception seen by reviewers cannot be independently matched.', [e['record_id'] for e in imports] + [claim['record_id']], 'freshness'))
    return {'subject_type': subject_type, 'subject_id': subject, 'revision': revision,
            'required_roles': required, 'selected_decisions': selections, 'findings': findings,
            'imports': imports, 'status': status(findings)}

"""End-to-end projection, schema, sealed chain and adversarial operator tests."""
from copy import deepcopy
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from operator_delivery import build as b
from reconciliation import reconcile as r
from validation import validate as v

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ACQUISITION = ROOT / 'artifacts/runs/omega4-live-20261020-attempt002'
NORMALIZED = ROOT / 'artifacts/normalizations/omega4-attempt002-normalization-v1'
VALIDATED = ROOT / 'artifacts/validations/omega4-attempt002-policy-validation-v1'
RECONCILED = ROOT / 'artifacts/reconciliations/omega4-attempt002-finance-reconciliation-v1'


class OperatorDeliveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        cls.addClassCleanup(cls.temp.cleanup)
        cls.output = Path(cls.temp.name) / 'run'
        with patch('socket.create_connection', side_effect=AssertionError('Offline replay must not access the network')):
            cls.sealed = b.build(ACQUISITION, NORMALIZED, VALIDATED, RECONCILED, cls.output, 'operator-test-v1')
        cls.snapshots = [json.loads((cls.output / f'batches/{i:03}.json').read_bytes()) for i in range(1, 5)]
        cls.queues = [json.loads((cls.output / f'queue/{i:03}.json').read_bytes()) for i in range(1, 5)]
        cls.doc = json.loads((NORMALIZED / 'records.v1.json').read_bytes())
        cls.report = json.loads((NORMALIZED / 'parsing-report.v1.json').read_bytes())
        cls.validation = json.loads((VALIDATED / 'findings.v1.json').read_bytes())

    def claim(self, ident, batch=4, value=None):
        return next(c for c in (value or self.snapshots[batch - 1])['claims'] if c['claim_id'] == ident)

    def projected_mutation(self, change):
        doc = deepcopy(self.doc); change(doc)
        result = r.evaluate(doc, self.report, self.validation, 4)
        processes, work = b.cancellation_projection(doc, result, self.snapshots[2]['travel_cancellations'])
        active = b.active_work(doc, result, work)
        return b.snapshot(result, doc, self.report, 'isolated-test', self.snapshots[-1]['source_binding'],
                          self.snapshots[-1]['predecessor'], self.snapshots[-1]['queue_binding'], active, processes)

    def test_four_snapshots_schema_chain_and_exact_final_inventory(self):
        self.assertEqual(b.verify(self.output)['verified_snapshots'], 4)
        self.assertEqual([s['batch_id'] for s in self.snapshots], ['001', '002', '003', '004'])
        self.assertIsNone(self.snapshots[0]['predecessor'])
        for index, snap in enumerate(self.snapshots):
            b.check_snapshot(snap)
            if index:
                previous = self.output / f'batches/{index:03}.json'
                self.assertEqual(snap['predecessor'], {'path': str(previous.relative_to(self.output)), 'sha256': v.digest(previous.read_bytes())})
        self.assertEqual((len(self.snapshots[-1]['claims']), len(self.snapshots[-1]['claim_revision_history'])), (121, 127))
        self.assertEqual(self.snapshots[-1]['summary']['expense_occurrences'], 208)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.snapshots[-1]['admitted_event_ids']), 219)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.snapshots[-1]['request_facts']), 104)

    def test_source_bytes_and_non_native_provenance_preserved(self):
        self.assertEqual((self.output / 'acquisition-manifest.original.json').read_bytes(), (ACQUISITION / 'sources.json').read_bytes())
        for p in ACQUISITION.rglob('*'):
            if p.is_file() and p.name != 'sources.json':
                self.assertEqual((self.output / p.relative_to(ACQUISITION)).read_bytes(), p.read_bytes())
        source = json.loads((self.output / 'sources.json').read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(source['replay_mode'], 'offline-retained-replay')
        self.assertEqual(source['acquisition_run_id'], 'omega4-live-20261020-attempt002')
        self.assertEqual(next(f for f in source['files'] if f['source_id'] == 'policy')['status'], 'unavailable')
        self.assertIsNone(source['case_clock'])

    def test_csv_unknown_money_blank_held_and_known_personal_zero(self):
        with (self.output / 'claims.csv').open(newline='') as stream:
            reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
            self.assertEqual(reader.fieldnames, b.CSV_FIELDS)
            rows = list(reader)
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 121)
        self.assertTrue(all(x['status'] == 'held' and x['paid_cents'] == '' and x['balance_cents'] == '' for x in rows))

# Business dispositions and financial holds

The current interim result is
[the business-disposition shared-blocker report](../artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-shared-blockers-v1/report.md),
with [case views](../artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-shared-blockers-v1/cases.md)
and [the unchanged-column CSV](../artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-shared-blockers-v1/claims.csv).
Decisions 001–004 remain binding and unchanged. This correction supplies no new
stakeholder answer, review, Finance authority, payment or financial closure.

`business_disposition` accompanies each claim/revision through validation,
reconciliation, snapshots and case views. Its value is `withdrawn`, `rejected`,
or null (unresolved). It contains an explicit reason, exact normalized source
references, admitted decision IDs and scope. Snapshot/source indexes resolve
references to retained source hashes and pages or workbook rows. C13/r1's binder
page 13 records withdrawal; C14/r1's admitted budget-owner decision and matching
packet at workbook row 40 record rejection. No later retained revision reverses
either. These are current within retained evidence, not independently verified
external completeness. The October 20 policy copy, lines 22–26, separates such
business evidence from financial closure.

Withdrawal requires an explicit revision-specific source status and reason.
Rejection requires existing current-subject/revision, actor/role, source-version
and packet admission, followed by unambiguous current role selection. Conflicting
business evidence remains unresolved. A new revision does not inherit an old
withdrawal/rejection. Missing reviews or Finance events supply no disposition.
A generic submitted status is not converted into approval or a terminal result.

Financial `status` stays `held` in snapshots and CSV. CSV reasons and reports show
supported dispositions separately. Missing merchant proof, reviews, Finance
allocation and Decision 001 holds stay visible, with the same repair IDs/history
and owners. Gross/policy arithmetic is unchanged, unknown money stays unknown,
and neither rejection nor withdrawal is proof of a zero financial effect.

## Current verification and replay

From the repository root, select a locally provisioned Python 3.10+ interpreter
as `OPERATOR_PYTHON`, with `operator_delivery/requirements.txt` and its transitive
dependencies installed. No downloads or network are needed. See
[offline environment instructions](shared-blockers.md#offline-python-environment).
Current outputs bind current code/schema/documentation and verify directly:

```sh
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.build verify artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-operator-v1
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.build verify artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-containment-v1
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.shared_blockers verify artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-shared-blockers-v1
```

For a new replay, choose a fresh external temporary directory. Never reuse a
sealed artifact path. Run these commands sequentially: build exit 2 means a
successfully retained partial result with unresolved work, not a failure to write;
exit 1 means failure. Verification exit 0 certifies implemented checks only.

```sh
DISPOSITION_REPLAY=$(mktemp -d)
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m validation.validate --run artifacts/runs/omega4-live-20261020-attempt002 --normalized artifacts/normalizations/omega4-attempt002-normalization-v1 --output "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/validation"
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m reconciliation.reconcile --run artifacts/runs/omega4-live-20261020-attempt002 --normalized artifacts/normalizations/omega4-attempt002-normalization-v1 --validated "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/validation" --output "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/reconciliation"
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.build build --acquisition artifacts/runs/omega4-live-20261020-attempt002 --normalized artifacts/normalizations/omega4-attempt002-normalization-v1 --validated "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/validation" --reconciled "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/reconciliation" --output "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/containment" --run-id disposition-replay --dependency-containment --prior-operator artifacts/runs/omega4-attempt002-containment-v2
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.shared_blockers build --source-run "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/containment" --output "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/shared-blockers" --run-id disposition-shared-replay
"$OPERATOR_PYTHON" -B -m operator_delivery.shared_blockers verify "$DISPOSITION_REPLAY/shared-blockers"
```

Prior runs remain immutable, with their original snapshot links and hashes.
Their historical code/schema/documentation bindings differ from current ones;
restoring old documentation alone is insufficient to execute historical replay.
Use matching historical implementation versions for semantic verification.
New containment output retains the preceding containment repair register and
manifest byte-for-byte as historical evidence. New runs replay all four arrival
boundaries; they do not append a fictitious fifth delivery to an earlier chain.

Native Notion completeness, package definitions, packet entitlement evidence,
financial allocation and existing repairs remain unresolved. A successful local
verification is neither external operator acceptance nor financial completion.

withdrawal/rejection. Missing reviews or Finance events supply no disposition.

supported dispositions separately. Missing merchant proof, reviews, Finance
allocation and Decision 001 holds stay visible, with the same repair IDs/history
and owners. Gross/policy arithmetic is unchanged, unknown money stays unknown,
and neither rejection nor withdrawal is proof of a zero financial effect.

as `OPERATOR_PYTHON`, with `operator_delivery/requirements.txt` and its transitive

"""Relocated preservation verification without access to the original checkout."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PACKAGE = Path('artifacts/verifications/omega4-attempt002-business-disposition-portability-v1')


class PreservationPortabilityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='omega4-relocated-')
        cls.addClassCleanup(cls.temp.cleanup)
        cls.cwd = Path(cls.temp.name)
        cls.checkout = cls.cwd / 'different checkout' / 'repository'
        shutil.copytree(ROOT, cls.checkout,
                        ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('.git', '.entire', '.codex', '__pycache__'))

    def run_verifier(self):
        # Path reads may only use the relocated repository. An accidental
        # original-checkout or shared /tmp baseline fallback must fail, even
        # when those files happen to exist on the test machine.
        runner = '''
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import sys
root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
original_open = Path.open
def guarded_open(path, *args, **kwargs):
    if not path.resolve().is_relative_to(root):
        raise PermissionError("Read outside relocated checkout: " + str(path))
    return original_open(path, *args, **kwargs)
Path.open = guarded_open
runpy.run_path(sys.argv[2], run_name="__main__")
'''
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, '-I', '-B', '-c', runner, str(self.checkout),
             str(self.checkout / PACKAGE / 'verify-preservation.py')],
            cwd=self.cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)

    def test_relocated_checkout_uses_only_packaged_evidence(self):
        result = self.run_verifier()
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        report = json.loads(result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((report['checks'], report['verified_snapshot_chains'],
                          report['verified_snapshots']), ('passed', 3, 12))
        self.assertEqual((report['final_financial_holds'], report['actual_financial_closures']), (121, 0))
        self.assertEqual(report['final_repair_states'],
                         {'open': 582, 'cleared_by_recheck': 218, 'superseded': 45})

    def test_missing_packaged_baseline_has_no_external_fallback(self):
        baseline = self.checkout / PACKAGE / 'preservation-baseline.json'
        saved = baseline.read_bytes()
        baseline.unlink()
        try:
            result = self.run_verifier()
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn('preservation-baseline.json', result.stderr)
        finally:
            baseline.write_bytes(saved)

    def test_changed_packaged_baseline_is_rejected(self):
        baseline = self.checkout / PACKAGE / 'preservation-baseline.json'
        saved = baseline.read_bytes()
        baseline.write_text('{}')
        try:
            result = self.run_verifier()
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn('differs from the original sealed baseline', result.stderr)
        finally:
            baseline.write_bytes(saved)

+Employees claim actual paid transport, conference, lodging and meal costs. A receipt describes a purchase; a linked settled merchant transaction proves employee payment. Match employee, trip, cost ID, currency and gross amount. Tax included in the gross amount is treated as cost; corporate VAT recovery is outside this workflow. Personal purchases have zero entitlement. An unknown category, missing evidence, missing rate or missing applicable cap is unresolved, never an assumed zero.

+Transport and conference have no category cap. Lodging uses the supplied cap per night; meals use the supplied cap per day. For each line, allowed original amount = min(supported gross amount, applicable cap × documented units); transport/conference use supported gross amount. Caps are in the expense currency for the destination and employee-payment date. Units are positive integers. No per diem or automatic allowance is payable. Apply Finance's exact payment-date EUR-per-currency-unit rate; EUR uses 1. Round each converted line to EUR cents using decimal half-up; sum rounded line amounts. Finance can issue an explicit, version-bound exception with a replacement allowed amount and reason; neither the employee nor automation invents one. Each supplied exception states actor, claim/revision, cost, replacement allowed original amount, reason and covered_issues

+Domestic trips do not need a permit. An international trip needs its own approved permit before the first arrangement/payment commitment. Permit administration, budget owner and supervisor review the trip estimate. Claim administration, budget owner and supervisor separately review actual reimbursement. A director additionally reviews amounts strictly above EUR 1,000.00 (reviewed estimate for permit, reviewed entitlement for claim). Exactly EUR 1,000.00 does not require a director. When budget owner and supervisor are the same stable person, one response with both roles satisfies those two positions for that subject/version. Administration and director never collapse into another role. A permit response never approves a claim. A late permit does not retroactively authorize travel arrangements; Finance may explicitly resolve reimbursement eligibility while the permit exception remains recorded.

+Costs may be claimed as soon as the employee has paid, including before travel. After acceptance/dispatch retain the original request basis and hold competing replacements until supplied Finance status/cancellation/adjustment resolves the obligation. Only Finance accepted/adjustment/cancelled facts change accepted commitments; business confirmation cannot release them. After reimbursement reopen reconciliation; explicit current cost disposition and reviews, any needed linked confirmed refund and Finance resolution must agree before closure. Only the confirmed refund reduces net paid. Continue observing original requests after cancellation or claim reassignment, including late transfers. Maintain separate cancellation state and event references for every observed valid process, including trips with no claim; retain affected claim and original request links, unresolved/no-financial-effect/resolved consequence and next owner. Smaller repositories are faster to clone and easier to work with and maintain. If your repository excessively impacts our infrastructure, you might receive an email from GitHub Support asking you to take corrective action. L54: You can prevent your repository from impacting our infrastructure by effectively managing your repository's size and overall health. You can find advice and a tool for repository analysis in the cite14†`github/git-sizer`†github.com repository.

L56: Git is not designed to serve as a backup tool. However, there are many solutions specifically designed for performing backups, such as cite18†Arq†www.arqbackup.com , cite19†Carbonite†www.carbonite.com , and cite20†CrashPlan†www.crashplan.com .

L62: ### cite21†Removing a file added in the most recent unpushed commit L63: 
L64: If the file was added with your most recent commit, and you have not pushed to GitHub.com, you can delete the file and amend the commit:

L74:     `

L80:     # to remove the file from the unpushed history as well
L81:     `

L83:   5. Push your commits to GitHub.com:

L19: Learn how to work around the 2 GiB push limit.
L20: 
L21: Copy markdown
L22: 
L23: ## In this article
L24: 
L25:   * cite3†About the push limit L26: 
L27:   * cite4†Splitting up a large push L28: 
L29:   * cite5†Starting from scratch L30: ## cite3†About the push limit L31: 
L32: GitHub has a maximum 2 GiB limit for a single push. You might hit this limit when trying to upload very large repositories for the first time, importing large repositories from other platforms, or when trying to rewrite the history of large existing repositories.
L33: 
L34: If you hit this limit, you may see one of the following error messages:
L35: 
L36:   * `fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly`
L37:   * `remote: fatal: pack exceeds maximum allowed size`
L38: You can either split up your push into smaller parts, or delete the Git history and start from scratch. If you have made a single commit that's larger than 2 GiB and you can't delete the Git history and start from scratch, then you will need to perform an interactive rebase to split the large commit into multiple smaller ones.
L39: ## cite4†Splitting up a large push L40: 
L41: You can avoid hitting the limit by breaking your push into smaller parts, each of which should be under 2 GiB in size. If a branch is within this size limit, you can push it all at once. However, if a branch is larger than 2 GiB, you'll need to split the push into even smaller portions and push only a few commits at a time.
L42: 
L43:   1. If you haven't configured the remote yet, add the repository as a new remote. For more information, see cite6†Managing remote repositories .
L44:   2. To find suitable commits spread out along the history of the main branch in your local repository, run the following command:
L45: 
L46:     `git log --oneline --reverse refs/heads/BRANCH-NAME | awk 'NR % 1000 == 0'
L47:     `
L48: 
L49: This command reveals every 1000th commit. You can increase or decrease the number to adjust the step size.
L50: 
L51:   3. Push each of these commits one at a time to your GitHub hosted repository.
L52: 
L53:     `git push REMOTE-NAME +<YOUR_COMMIT_SHA_NUMBER>:refs/heads/BRANCH-NAME
L54:     `
L55: If you see the message `remote: fatal: pack exceeds maximum allowed size`, reduce the step size in step 2 and try again.
L56: 
L57:   4. Go through the same process for every commit you identified in the history from step 2.
L58: 
L59:   5. If this is the first time this repository is being pushed to GitHub, perform a final mirror push to ensure any remaining refs are pushed up.
L60: 
L61:     `git push REMOTE-NAME --mirror
L62:     `
L63: 
L64: If this is still too large, you'll need to push up other branches in stages using the same steps.
L65: Once you're familiar with the procedure, you can automate steps 2 to 4 to simplify the process. For example:
L66: 
L67:     `step_commits=$(git log --oneline --reverse refs/heads/BRANCH-NAME | awk 'NR % 1000 == 0')
L68:     echo "$step_commits" | while read commit message; do git push REMOTE-NAME +$commit:refs/heads/BRANCH-NAME; done
L69:     `
L70: ## cite5†Starting from scratch L71: 
L72: If the repository does not have any history, or your initial commit was over 2 GiB on its own and you don't mind resetting the Git history, you can also start from scratch.
L73: 
L74:   1. On your local copy, delete the hidden `.git` folder to remove all the previous Git history and convert it back into a normal folder full of files.
L75: 
L76:   2. Create a new empty folder.
L77: 
L78:   3. Run `git init` and `git lfs install` on the new folder, and add the new empty GitHub repository as a remote.
L79:   4. If you already use Git Large File Storage and have all of the Git LFS tracking rules you intend to use already listed in the `.gitattributes` file in the old folder, that should be the first file you copy across to the new folder. You should ensure the tracking rules are in place before you add any other files, so that there's no chance things intended for Git LFS will be committed to regular Git storage.
L80: If you do not already use Git LFS, you can skip this step, or you can set up the tracking rules you intend to use in the `.gitattributes` file in the new folder before you copy any other files across. For more information, see cite7†Configuring Git Large File Storage .
L81:   5. Move batches of files that are smaller than 2 GiB from the old folder to the new folder. After each batch is moved, create a commit and push it before moving the next batch. You can take a cautious approach and stick to around 2 GiB. Alternatively, if you have a folder with files meant for Git LFS, you can ignore those files when considering the 2 GiB limit per batch.
L82: Once the old folder is empty, the GitHub repository should contain everything. If you are using Git LFS, all files meant for Git LFS should be pushed to Git LFS storage.
